questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair (railway zone and headquarters) from the following.

options.text: South - East Central Railway Zone – Bilaspur

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Railway Zone - Kolkata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central Railway Zone** has its headquarters in **Mumbai**, not Kolkata.
 
• The **South - East Central Railway Zone** has its headquarters in **Bilaspur**.
 
• The **North Western Railway Zone** has its headquarters in **Jaipur**.
 
• The **South Western Railway Zone** has its headquarters in **Hubli**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Central Railway Zone is one of the oldest zones in Indian Railways, and it was formed on 5th November 1951.
 
• The headquarters of the Central Railway Zone is located at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) in Mumbai.
 
• Indian Railways is divided into 18 zones, and each zone is further divided into divisions.
 
• The zones and their respective headquarters are crucial for the administrative and operational efficiency of Indian Railways.
 
• Knowing the correct headquarters of each railway zone is essential for various competitive exams and general knowledge.

questions.question: Which of the following Ministers introduced the Central Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill 2023 and the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill 2023 in the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nirmala Sitharaman**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nirmala Sitharaman** introduced the Central Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill 2023 and the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill 2023 in the Lok Sabha.
 
• She is the **Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs** of India.
 
• The amendment bills aim to bring changes to the existing GST framework to streamline tax administration and compliance.
 
• The introduction of these bills is part of the government's ongoing efforts to simplify and improve the Goods and Services Tax regime in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** was implemented in India on 1st July 2017, replacing multiple indirect taxes previously levied by the central and state governments.
 
• GST is a **comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax** that is levied on every value addition.
 
• The GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, is responsible for making recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, and other related matters.
 
• The GST regime aims to create a **unified national market** by removing tax barriers between states and ensuring a seamless flow of goods and services.
 
• The Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) and Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) are two of the four components of GST, the other two being State Goods and Services Tax (SGST) and Union Territory Goods and Services Tax (UTGST).

questions.question: Who was the leader of the temple entry movement in 1930 at Kalaram temple, Nashik?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. BR Ambedkar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. BR Ambedkar** was the leader of the temple entry movement in 1930 at Kalaram temple, Nashik.
 
• The movement was aimed at allowing Dalits to enter the temple and perform their religious duties.
 
• It was part of the broader struggle against caste discrimination and for the rights of the untouchables.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar, a prominent social reformer and the principal architect of the Indian Constitution, led numerous movements for the upliftment of the marginalized communities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. BR Ambedkar** was born on 14th April 1891 and was a jurist, economist, politician, and social reformer.
 
• He played a crucial role in the Dalit Buddhist movement and campaigned against social discrimination towards the untouchables (Dalits).
 
• In 1956, he converted to Buddhism, initiating mass conversions of Dalits.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1990.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar's legacy continues to inspire movements for social justice and equality in India.

questions.question: Narmada Bachao Andolan (Save Narmada Movement) is a/an ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Social movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narmada Bachao Andolan (Save Narmada Movement)** is a social movement spearheaded by activists fighting for the rights of people affected by the construction of large dams on the Narmada River.
 
• This movement primarily focuses on the issues of displacement, rehabilitation, and environmental protection.
 
• The movement began in the mid-1980s and has garnered support from various national and international organizations.
 
• The primary aim is to ensure that the displaced people receive proper rehabilitation and compensation and to raise awareness about the environmental impacts of large dam projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Narmada River is one of the major rivers in central India, flowing westwards over a length of approximately 1,312 kilometers.
 
• Several large dams, including the Sardar Sarovar Dam, have been planned and constructed on the river, leading to significant socio-economic and environmental debates.
 
• The movement has been led by prominent activists such as Medha Patkar and has seen significant participation from local communities, NGOs, and environmentalists.
 
• While the movement has faced numerous challenges, it has also brought the issues of sustainable development and human rights to the forefront of public discourse in India.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Golgi apparatus?

options.text: Sorting and packaging of cellular products

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sorting and packaging of cellular products**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sorting and packaging of cellular products** is the primary function of the Golgi apparatus.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is an essential organelle in the cell, involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• It is often referred to as the cell's "post office" because it is responsible for directing molecular traffic.
 
• The Golgi apparatus also plays a role in the creation of lysosomes, which are involved in the breakdown of cellular waste.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Golgi apparatus was discovered by Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in 1898.
 
• It consists of a series of flattened membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
 
• Proteins and lipids enter the Golgi apparatus on the cis face and exit on the trans face after being processed.
 
• In addition to its role in packaging and sorting, the Golgi apparatus is also involved in the transport of lipids around the cell and the creation of lysosomes.
 
• Malfunctions in the Golgi apparatus can lead to diseases, including some forms of muscular dystrophy and neurodegenerative disorders.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India provides measures to ensure the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Constitution of India provides measures to ensure the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• It grants the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court (and High Courts) to seek justice when they feel that their Fundamental Rights have been violated.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar referred to this article as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.
 
• Article 32 is a fundamental right in itself and provides a powerful remedy for the enforcement of other Fundamental Rights.
 
• It empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which organelle contains enzymes for digesting cellular waste and foreign materials?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosome** is the organelle that contains enzymes for digesting cellular waste and foreign materials.
 
• Lysosomes are often referred to as the **"digestive system"** of the cell due to their role in breaking down unwanted substances.
 
• They contain a variety of **hydrolytic enzymes** that can degrade proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids.
 
• These enzymes function optimally at an acidic pH, which is maintained within the lysosome.
 
• Lysosomes play a crucial role in cellular processes such as **autophagy** (self-digestion of the cell's own components) and **apoptosis** (programmed cell death).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **nucleus** is the control center of the cell but does not contain digestive enzymes.
 
• The **mitochondrion** is known as the powerhouse of the cell, generating ATP, but it does not digest cellular waste.
 
• The **vacuole** is involved in storage and maintaining cellular homeostasis but is not primarily responsible for digestion.
 
• Lysosomes are formed by the budding off of vesicles from the **Golgi apparatus**.
 
• Defects in lysosomal function can lead to various diseases, known as **lysosomal storage disorders**.

questions.question: To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired our national struggle for freedom is a ______ fundamental duty in the list of fundamental duties enshrined in our Indian Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**second**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired our national struggle for freedom is the **second** fundamental duty listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The fundamental duties are enshrined in Article 51A under Part IVA of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• The fundamental duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they should also be conscious of the duties they owe to their country, society, and fellow citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Constitution originally did not contain a chapter on fundamental duties.
 
• There are currently **11 fundamental duties** listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties are not enforceable by law; however, they are considered essential for the promotion of a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• Some of the other fundamental duties include respecting the national symbols, protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India, and promoting harmony and brotherhood among all citizens.

questions.question: Which compound is used to neutralise fatty acids and convert them into salts in a process called saponification?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydroxide**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium hydroxide** is used to neutralise fatty acids and convert them into salts in the process called saponification.
 
• Saponification is a process that produces soap from fats or oils and a base.
 
• The reaction involves the hydrolysis of triglycerides (fatty acids) by sodium hydroxide to produce glycerol and soap.
 
• This process is essential in the production of various cleaning products and has been used for centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium hydroxide**, also known as lye or caustic soda, is a highly caustic metallic base and alkali.
 
• It is used in various industries including paper manufacturing, textiles, and cleaning agents.
 
• The chemical formula for sodium hydroxide is **NaOH**.
 
• Due to its corrosive nature, it must be handled with care, using appropriate safety measures.

questions.question: In 1800, which of the following experimental achievements was made by William Nicholson?

options.text: Discovery of low - cost filters for polarizing light

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Discovery of water electrolysis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Discovery of water electrolysis** was a significant experimental achievement made by William Nicholson in 1800.
 
• This discovery involved the decomposition of water (H₂O) into oxygen (O₂) and hydrogen gas (H₂) through the application of electric current.
 
• It was a foundational experiment in the field of electrochemistry and demonstrated the potential of electricity to induce chemical reactions.
 
• Nicholson's work laid the groundwork for further scientific exploration and technological advancements involving electrolysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William Nicholson** was an English chemist and inventor who made significant contributions to the field of science in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
 
• The process of water electrolysis is now widely used in various industrial applications, including the production of hydrogen fuel.
 
• Electrolysis is also employed in the extraction of metals from their ores and in electroplating processes.
 
• The discovery of water electrolysis marked a pivotal moment in the understanding of the relationship between electricity and chemical reactions.

questions.question: Arachnids belong to which subphylum of the phylum Arthropoda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chelicerata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arachnids** belong to the subphylum **Chelicerata** within the phylum Arthropoda.
 
• This subphylum includes a diverse group of arthropods such as spiders, scorpions, mites, and ticks.
 
• Chelicerates are characterized by the presence of chelicerae, which are specialized mouthparts used for feeding.
 
• Unlike other arthropods, chelicerates do not possess antennae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phylum **Arthropoda** is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, encompassing insects, arachnids, myriapods, and crustaceans.
 
• **Arthropods** are characterized by their exoskeleton, segmented bodies, and jointed appendages.
 
• The subphylum **Chelicerata** is divided into two main classes: Arachnida and Merostomata (horseshoe crabs).
 
• Arachnids play crucial roles in ecosystems as predators, controlling insect populations, and as prey for larger animals.

questions.question: Private income minus tax payment minus non - tax payment will give us the estimate for ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**personal disposable income**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Personal disposable income** is the amount of money that households have available for spending and saving after accounting for income taxes and non-tax payments.
 
• It is calculated by subtracting **tax payments and non-tax payments** from the **private income**.
 
• This measure is crucial as it reflects the actual purchasing power of individuals and households.
 
• Personal disposable income is an important indicator of the overall economic health and consumer spending capacity of a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Private income** includes all income earned by individuals and entities in the private sector, including wages, salaries, rent, interest, and profits.
 
• Non-tax payments can include items such as fines, fees, and other compulsory payments that are not classified as taxes.
 
• Understanding personal disposable income helps in analyzing consumer behavior, savings rates, and the overall economic activity within a country.
 
• Governments may use this metric to design fiscal policies aimed at stimulating economic growth and improving the standard of living.
 
• In macroeconomic terms, it is a key variable in the consumption function, which is used to model and predict consumer spending.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Newton** is the SI unit of force.
 
• The SI unit system is an international system of units that is widely used for scientific and technical measurements.
 
• Force is a vector quantity that has both magnitude and direction.
 
• It is measured in terms of the amount of acceleration it can give to a mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The SI unit of force, Newton, is named after Sir Isaac Newton in recognition of his work on classical mechanics.
 
 
• One Newton is defined as the force required to accelerate a one-kilogram mass by one meter per second squared.
 
• Force can be calculated using Newton's second law of motion: **F = ma (Force = mass × acceleration).**
 
• The concept of force is fundamental in physics and engineering, affecting various fields such as mechanics, electromagnetism, and thermodynamics.

questions.question: ______ is referred to as paper taxes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gift tax**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gift tax** is commonly referred to as paper taxes.
 
• Gift tax is a tax on the transfer of property by one individual to another while receiving nothing or less than full value in return.
 
• This tax is imposed on the donor, not the recipient.
 
• The term "paper taxes" is used because the transactions are often documented on paper, such as in the case of gifts of cash, stocks, or other assets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Gift Tax Act was introduced in India in 1958 but was abolished in 1998. However, gifts are now taxed under the Income Tax Act, 1961.
 
• Gifts exceeding a certain value received from non-relatives are taxable as income under the head "Income from Other Sources".
 
• Gifts received on occasions such as marriage or from specified relatives are exempt from tax.
 
• The taxability of gifts is an important aspect of financial planning and estate management.
